input.step_by_step_reasoning: 1) Inventory: the board shows a central AWS account (Security Engineers, QuickSight, Athena, a hand-drawn S3 findings bucket, MySQL, Glue, Macie) and two further AWS accounts, each with Macie and S3. 2) Pruning: Security Engineers is a generic human actor with no arrows, so it is removed. 3) Fusion: the three Macie icons act as one multi-account Macie deployment (production accounts connected to Macie), so they are fused into one node. The two member-account S3 icons are fused into one 'production S3 buckets' node (the scan targets). The central hand-drawn bucket is kept separate because it plays a different role (findings/results bucket). 4) MySQL is not an AWS service icon, so it is typed ThirdParty ('MySQL data lake'). 5) Edges from drawn arrows: Macie -> findings S3, Athena -> findings S3 (query), QuickSight -> findings S3 (the speaker says this is done via Athena), findings S3 -> MySQL. 6) Edges from the audio only: production S3 buckets -> Macie (Macie inventories and scans the buckets), and findings S3 -> Glue (Glue automations get, load and aggregate the data). Glue has no drawn arrow, so the Glue edge is an interpretation of the transcript. 7) Flows: flow 0 = discovery and findings delivery; flow 1 = query and dashboarding; flow 2 = load/aggregation into the MySQL data lake for remediation reporting.

graph.name: Oportun: Sensitive Data Discovery and DSPM with Amazon Macie
graph.notes: Multi-account Amazon Macie scans production S3 buckets for sensitive member data (SSNs, ITINs, government IDs). Findings (metadata only, no PII) land in a company-owned S3 bucket, are queried with Athena, visualized in QuickSight, and loaded into a MySQL data lake with Glue automations to identify bucket owners and remediate. Reported accuracy of automated sensitive data discovery for patterns such as SSNs and ITINs is 95%.

nodes.name: Production S3 Buckets (member AWS accounts)
nodes.notes: S3 buckets in the connected production AWS accounts. Macie inventories them and the team selects which ones to scan. Fused from the two member-account S3 icons.

nodes.name: Amazon Macie
nodes.notes: Data discovery tool connected across multiple AWS accounts, with production accounts prioritized. Quickly inventories all S3 buckets and runs manual or scheduled scans. Automated sensitive data discovery accuracy is 95% for patterns/regexes such as SSNs and ITINs. Fused from the three Macie icons.

nodes.name: Amazon S3 (Macie findings bucket)
nodes.notes: Company-owned bucket set up per connected account to receive Macie results. Holds only metadata (e.g. number of SSNs per bucket); no PII or sensitive data.

nodes.name: Amazon Athena
nodes.notes: SQL-based query tool that looks into the findings buckets and queries the findings information.

nodes.name: Amazon QuickSight
nodes.notes: Dashboards showing the top 10/20/30 risky buckets by PII type and their owners, used to drive remediation. Other BI tools such as Tableau or Power BI could be used instead.

nodes.name: MySQL
nodes.notes: MySQL data lake built by the company, into which findings data is dropped to identify bucket owners and support remediation.

nodes.name: AWS Glue
nodes.notes: Automations that get, load and aggregate the findings data for reporting to data owners. No arrow is drawn to it on the board.

edges.notes: Macie inventories and scans the selected production S3 buckets (manual or scheduled) for sensitive data. From the audio; no arrow drawn.
Macie writes scan findings (metadata only, e.g. counts of SSNs per bucket) to the findings S3 bucket.
Athena queries the findings stored in the S3 bucket with SQL.
QuickSight reads the findings from the S3 bucket (via Athena, per the speaker) to build dashboards of risky buckets by PII type and owner.
Glue automations get, load and aggregate the findings data. From the audio; no arrow drawn.
Findings data is dropped into the MySQL data lake for owner identification and remediation reporting.
